meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('classic, classical').

examples.text: Сегодня у шефа очень классический день в ресторане.
examples.trans: Today the chef is having a very classic day at the restaurant.

meanings.note: Question word and conjunction. Core Russian adv meaning 'when' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.

meanings.note: мам! = casual 'Mum!' when calling her
Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to find', paired with 'находить'.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?
examples.trans: Well, where am I going to find movers right now?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

Locative на носу. Common masculine noun meaning 'nose' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Когда не можешь сам себе нос вытереть.
examples.trans: When you can't even wipe your own nose yourself.

examples.text: От холода у него покраснел нос.
examples.trans: His nose turned red from the cold.

examples.text: У меня скоро долгожданная пенсия на носу.
examples.trans: My long-awaited pension is right around the corner.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нам очень дорого обходится авторская кухня.
examples.trans: Auteur cuisine costs us very dearly.

examples.text: Это все, кто выходил из отеля.
examples.trans: That is everyone who left the hotel.
What is going on here right now?

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'they' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'влекать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to distract'.

examples.text: Ладно, не буду тебя отвлекать сейчас.
examples.trans: Alright, I will not distract you right now.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и отвлекать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to distract on time.

meanings.en: to think it over, to give it a thought
meanings.note: Once, for a while. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'умать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think (it over)', paired with 'думать'.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

полениться.gloss: to be too lazy, hesitate to make an effort

meanings.en: to be lazy, spare the effort
meanings.note: не поленился = did not hesitate, took the trouble

examples.text: Чужой человек из Москвы не поленился.
examples.trans: A complete stranger from Moscow took the trouble.
He took the trouble to walk on foot.

meanings.note: On foot, once. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come, to arrive', paired with 'приходить'.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: an election programme, a TV programme
Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'грамма'). Common feminine noun meaning 'programme' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The programme will be on the website.
Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: просить прощения = to ask for forgiveness
Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask (for)', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.en: to have fun, to amuse oneself
meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'влекаться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to have fun'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: The children are having fun in the kitchen.
She is having fun there in the kitchen.

examples.text: А я смотрю, вы тут хорошо развлекаетесь.
examples.trans: And I see you are having good fun here.

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?
